title: Suppression of GOLM1 by EGCG through HGF/HGFR/AKT/GSK-3beta/beta-catenin/c-Myc signaling pathway inhibits cell migration of MDA-MB-231.
authors: Xie, Ling; Yi, Jun; Song, Yongjia; Zhao, Mengyao; Fan, Liqiang; Zhao, Liming
journal: Food and chemical toxicology : an international journal published for the British Industrial Biological Research Association
one_liner_zh: 研究EGCG通过HGF/HGFR/AKT/GSK-3β/β-catenin/c-Myc信号通路抑制GOLM1表达及乳腺癌细胞迁移，仅含分子对接预测，无蛋白质-DNA互作体系或AI/物理模拟方法，与本课题关联微弱。
abstract: Golgi Membrane Protein 1 (GOLM1) has been identified as a prime target for cancer therapy because it overexpresses in many solid tumors, increases tumor growth and metastasis and leads to unfavorable survival. Though various approaches including siRNA interference and antibody targeting have been attempted, GOLM1 has remained an un-targetable molecule because of its mainly intracellular location and the lack of domains that could possibly be interfered with by small molecules. Numerous natural anti-tumoral plant substances have been identified, while their possible function on GOLM1 has never been revealed. This is the first report to study the relationship between GOLM1 downregulation and natural anti-tumoral plant substances and the possible mechanism. Among three tested possible migration-inhibiting natural substances (Epigallocatechin gallate (EGCG), Betulinic acid (BA) and Lupeol), EGCG showed the most potent inhibition effect on GOLM1 expression and MDA-MB-231 cell migration. Knocking down GOLM1 expression further increased the EGCG treatment effect. Molecular docking prediction and following experiments suggested that EGCG may inhibit GOLM1 expression and MDA-MB-231 cells migration through HGF/HGFR/AKT/GSK-3/beta-catenin/c-Myc signaling pathway. In all, EGCG is the first identified GOLM1 downregulation natural product. Silencing GOLM1 may be a novel mechanism of potentiated anti-cancer migration effects and cytotoxic effect of EGCG. In addition, this study shed a new way for cancer therapy by combination of GOLM1 silencing and EGCG treatment in the future.
abstract_zh: 高尔基体膜蛋白1（GOLM1）已被确定为癌症治疗的主要靶点，因为它在多种实体瘤中过度表达，促进肿瘤生长和转移，并导致不良生存率。尽管已尝试了包括siRNA干扰和抗体靶向在内的多种方法，但由于GOLM1主要位于细胞内且缺乏可能被小分子干扰的结构域，它仍然是一个难以靶向的分子。已发现多种天然抗肿瘤植物物质，但它们对GOLM1的可能作用从未被揭示。这是首次研究GOLM1下调与天然抗肿瘤植物物质之间关系及其可能机制的报道。在测试的三种可能抑制迁移的天然物质（表没食子儿茶素没食子酸酯（EGCG）、桦木酸（BA）和羽扇豆醇）中，EGCG对GOLM1表达和MDA-MB-231细胞迁移表现出最强的抑制作用。敲低GOLM1表达进一步增强了EGCG的处理效果。分子对接预测及后续实验表明，EGCG可能通过HGF/HGFR/AKT/GSK-3/β-catenin/c-Myc信号通路抑制GOLM1表达和MDA-MB-231细胞迁移。总之，EGCG是首个被鉴定为下调GOLM1的天然产物。沉默GOLM1可能是增强EGCG抗肿瘤迁移效应和细胞毒性作用的新机制。此外，本研究为未来通过结合GOLM1沉默和EGCG治疗进行癌症治疗开辟了新途径。
